subtype: Approach: hiding the game and lying about homework [Pitfall]
passage: I am Aadhya, and I share a room with my brother Vihaan, so I saw it all. On Monday Vihaan told Mummy, "Homework is finished," and then took the game under his blanket with the sound turned low. He did it on Tuesday and Wednesday too. On Thursday, Alka Ma'am wrote in his diary that two assignments were missing. Mummy read the note twice. Vihaan's ears went red and he looked at the floor. "It is not only the marks," Mummy said quietly. "You told me it was done." The console went into the cupboard in her room for the week. Vihaan said nothing to me that night, and I could not tell if he was sorry or just cross.

qa.q: What did Alka Ma'am write in Vihaan's diary?
qa.a: She wrote that two assignments were missing.

qa.q: What might Vihaan have been feeling when Mummy read the note?
qa.a: Ashamed and worried, since his ears went red and he looked at the floor, though Aadhya cannot tell if he was sorry or just cross.

qa.q: What could Vihaan do to begin rebuilding Mummy's trust?
qa.a: Tell the truth about how much homework is left, finish the missing work and show it to her each evening, because steady honesty rebuilds trust.

qa.q: How might Mummy feel about Vihaan's words on Monday?
qa.a: Hurt and disappointed, since she said it was not only the marks and that he had told her the work was done.

grounding: A boy claims homework is done and plays in secret, and the teacher's note brings both a marks problem and lost trust.

passage:
Monday: "Homework done?" his mother, Sangeeta, asked. "Done," said Vishal, and went to his room, where he played his phone game under the blanket until nine.
Wednesday: He said it again. It wasn't. Two English worksheets and a maths page were stuffed, unfinished, at the bottom of his bag.
Friday: Sangeeta's phone buzzed during dinner. It was his class teacher: three assignments missing this week. She read the message twice and put the phone face down. She didn't shout. She just said, "You told me it was done. Twice." That weekend Vishal did all three assignments at the dining table, and the phone stayed with his mother. On Monday, when he said "Done", she opened his bag to check.

qa.q: What did the teacher's message say?
qa.a: Three assignments were missing this week.

qa.q: How might Vishal have felt when his mother said 'Twice'?
qa.a: Ashamed and guilty, caught in his own lie.

qa.q: What else could Vishal have done on Monday?
qa.a: Told the truth and asked for help with the worksheets, before the missing work piled up.
Quietly hurt; she doesn't shout, but she no longer takes his word and checks his bag.

grounding: Over a week, a boy lies about homework to play secretly, and the teacher's report brings both a marks problem and lost trust.

subtype: Approach: hiding the game and lying about homework [Pitfall]
passage: Pranav, you're hiding that phone under your pillow? Let me tell you what happened to me. When I was eleven, I, Lalit, had a small handheld game my uncle had brought back from abroad. Every evening I told my mother, "Homework finished," and played under the blanket with the sound off. For two weeks it worked. Then my class teacher sent a letter home: eight pieces of homework missing, marks cut, and would my parents please come to meet her. My mother read the letter at the kitchen table and didn't look at me for a long time. The marks I earned back, slowly. What took longer was her trust. For months she checked my notebook every night, and I knew I had earned that too.

qa.q: How many pieces of homework were missing?
How did young Lalit feel when his mother didn't look up for a long time?
qa.a: Ashamed, knowing the lie had hurt her.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story caused the most trouble?
qa.a: Saying 'Homework finished' when it wasn't; doing the homework before playing would have avoided both the marks and the lost trust.

qa.q: How might Lalit's mother have felt reading the letter?
qa.a: Hurt and disappointed, betrayed by the evenings of 'Homework finished'.

grounding: An elder recalls lying about homework to play in secret, and how the teacher's letter cost both marks and a parent's trust.
